# OopsMyPassword (https://oopsmypassword.web.app)

> Privacy-first cybersecurity tools, structured Academy courses (Cyber Security, OSINT, Pentesting, Web Application Security), OSINT & Pentest tool directories, CLI cheat sheets, and technical security guides. All interactive tools run 100% client-side in the browser with zero telemetry.

## Interactive Client-Side Security Tools
- [Password Strength Checker](https://oopsmypassword.web.app/checker): Real-time local entropy, pattern detection, and crack-time estimation.
- [CSPRNG Password Generator](https://oopsmypassword.web.app/generator): Generates random passwords using window.crypto.getRandomValues().
- [Breach Check (k-Anonymity Demo)](https://oopsmypassword.web.app/breach-check): Zero-knowledge 5-hex-character SHA-1 prefix range lookup.
- [Google Dork & OSINT Search Query Builder](https://oopsmypassword.web.app/dork-builder): Visual composer for site:, filetype:, inurl:, intitle:, and intext: queries with 24 presets.
- [Client-Side Hash, JWT & Encoding Inspector](https://oopsmypassword.web.app/hash-inspector): Offline WebCrypto SHA-256/384/512 calculator, password hash identifier, and JWT security auditor.
- [Phishing URL & Suspicious Link Risk Scanner](https://oopsmypassword.web.app/url-scanner): Lexical URL analyzer for IDN homograph punycode (xn--), @-authority confusion, and brand typosquatting.
- [Diceware Passphrase Generator](https://oopsmypassword.web.app/passphrase): Multi-word passphrases with exact bit-entropy calculation.
- [Password Entropy Calculator](https://oopsmypassword.web.app/entropy): Interactive character pool and keyspace calculator.
- [Password Health Audit](https://oopsmypassword.web.app/password-health): 10-point local credential hygiene check.
- [Security Checklist](https://oopsmypassword.web.app/security-checklist): 16-step account hardening tracker.

## Structured Academy Tracks & Hubs
- [OMP Academy Home](https://oopsmypassword.web.app/learning): 118+ interactive lessons with 4-question self-checks and Full/Step reader modes.
- [OSINT Hub](https://oopsmypassword.web.app/osint): 20+ OSINT investigation tools with interactive CLI builders and side-by-side comparison drawer.
- [Pentest Hub](https://oopsmypassword.web.app/pentest): Authorized penetration testing tools by phase with interactive CLI command builders.
- [Tool Comparisons Hub](https://oopsmypassword.web.app/compare): 15 head-to-head technical comparisons.
- [CLI Cheat Sheets Hub](https://oopsmypassword.web.app/cheatsheets): 10 interactive, printable command references.
- [Security Glossary](https://oopsmypassword.web.app/glossary): 30 foundational security, cryptography, and OSINT term deep-dives.
- [Articles & Security Research](https://oopsmypassword.web.app/articles): Long-form cybersecurity guides and threat analysis.

## Tool Comparisons
- [Bitwarden vs 1Password: Security & Vault Comparison](https://oopsmypassword.web.app/compare/bitwarden-vs-1password): Head-to-head comparison of Bitwarden and 1Password across encryption architecture, Secret Key defense, open-source auditing, self-hosting, and pricing.
- [Bitwarden vs Proton Pass: Privacy & Encryption Guide](https://oopsmypassword.web.app/compare/bitwarden-vs-proton-pass): Compare Bitwarden and Proton Pass across end-to-end metadata encryption, hide-my-email aliases, Argon2id key derivation, and Swiss privacy laws.
- [KeePassXC vs Bitwarden: Offline Vault vs Cloud Sync](https://oopsmypassword.web.app/compare/keepassxc-vs-bitwarden): Should you store passwords in a local offline KDBX 4.1 file with KeePassXC or a zero-knowledge cloud vault with Bitwarden? Threat model comparison.
- [YubiKey vs Synced Passkeys: FIDO2 Auth Comparison](https://oopsmypassword.web.app/compare/yubikey-vs-passkeys): Compare hardware security keys (YubiKey 5 / FIDO2 device-bound passkeys) against cloud-synced passkeys in Apple iCloud Keychain, Google, and Bitwarden.
- [Nmap vs Masscan: Network Port Scanner Comparison](https://oopsmypassword.web.app/compare/nmap-vs-masscan): Technical comparison of Nmap and Masscan across packet transmission architecture, service version fingerprinting, NSE scripting, and scan accuracy.
- [Burp Suite vs OWASP ZAP: Web Security Proxy Guide](https://oopsmypassword.web.app/compare/burp-suite-vs-owasp-zap): Compare Burp Suite and OWASP ZAP for manual HTTP request tampering, automated DAST CI/CD scanning, Intruder fuzzing, and extension ecosystems.
- [ffuf vs Gobuster: Web Fuzzing & Content Discovery](https://oopsmypassword.web.app/compare/ffuf-vs-gobuster): Compare ffuf and Gobuster for directory brute-forcing, virtual host enumeration, POST parameter fuzzing, auto-calibration, and response filtering.
- [sqlmap vs Manual SQL Injection Testing: Pentest Guide](https://oopsmypassword.web.app/compare/sqlmap-vs-manual-sqli): When should pentesters use automated sqlmap versus manual Boolean, time-based, and UNION SQL injection verification in Burp Repeater?
- [Sherlock vs Maigret: Username OSINT Tool Comparison](https://oopsmypassword.web.app/compare/sherlock-vs-maigret): Compare Sherlock and Maigret for username OSINT investigations across site coverage, profile metadata parsing, recursive handle pivoting, and HTML/PDF reporting.
- [OWASP Amass vs Subfinder: Subdomain Recon Comparison](https://oopsmypassword.web.app/compare/amass-vs-subfinder): Compare OWASP Amass and ProjectDiscovery Subfinder for passive subdomain discovery, ASN & BGP mapping, DNS brute-forcing, and Unix pipeline speed.
- [Shodan vs Censys: Internet Exposure Search Comparison](https://oopsmypassword.web.app/compare/shodan-vs-censys): Compare Shodan and Censys for external attack-surface discovery, TLS certificate hunting, ICS/IoT banner analysis, and origin IP discovery behind CDNs.
- [Wireshark vs tcpdump: Packet Capture & Analysis Guide](https://oopsmypassword.web.app/compare/wireshark-vs-tcpdump): Compare Wireshark and tcpdump for live network packet capture, BPF capture filters, display filter forensics, TLS decryption, and incident response.
- [TruffleHog vs Gitleaks: Secret Scanning Compared](https://oopsmypassword.web.app/compare/trufflehog-vs-gitleaks): Compare TruffleHog and Gitleaks for secret scanning: live credential verification, detection accuracy, git history coverage, custom rules, CI integration and the false-positive trade-off.
- [Gobuster vs Feroxbuster: Content Discovery Compared](https://oopsmypassword.web.app/compare/gobuster-vs-feroxbuster): Compare Gobuster and Feroxbuster for directory and content discovery: recursion, wildcard filtering, extension handling, link extraction, speed and where each one fits in a web assessment.
- [Nikto vs Nuclei: Web Server Scanning Compared](https://oopsmypassword.web.app/compare/nikto-vs-nuclei): Compare Nikto and Nuclei for web server and vulnerability scanning: check coverage, false positives, custom templates, concurrency, severity filtering and which scanner to run first.

## CLI Cheat Sheets
- [Nmap Command Cheat Sheet: Discovery, Stealth & NSE](https://oopsmypassword.web.app/cheatsheets/nmap-command-cheatsheet): Copy-ready Nmap CLI commands for host discovery, SYN/TCP/UDP port scanning, service fingerprinting, NSE vulnerability scripts, and output formats.
- [Google Dorks Cheat Sheet for OSINT & Bug Bounty Recon](https://oopsmypassword.web.app/cheatsheets/google-dorks-osint-cheatsheet): Essential Google search operators (site, filetype, inurl, intitle, intext) for discovering exposed configuration files, portals, and cloud buckets.
- [ffuf Web Fuzzing Cheat Sheet: Directories, Vhosts & APIs](https://oopsmypassword.web.app/cheatsheets/ffuf-web-fuzzing-cheatsheet): Practical ffuf one-liners for directory discovery, virtual host enumeration, GET/POST parameter fuzzing, auto-calibration, and rate limiting.
- [Wireshark Display Filters Cheat Sheet for Packet Analysis](https://oopsmypassword.web.app/cheatsheets/wireshark-display-filters-cheatsheet): High-signal Wireshark and tshark display filters for hunting suspicious HTTP requests, DNS tunneling, TLS handshakes, TCP anomalies, and SMB traffic.
- [sqlmap Cheat Sheet: Authorized SQL Injection Verification](https://oopsmypassword.web.app/cheatsheets/sqlmap-pentest-cheatsheet): Safe, controlled sqlmap flags for testing captured Burp HTTP requests, tuning --level and --risk, rate limiting, and verifying parameterization.
- [Linux Privilege Escalation Cheat Sheet: Enumeration & Hardening](https://oopsmypassword.web.app/cheatsheets/linux-privilege-escalation-cheatsheet): Essential Linux local enumeration commands for auditing sudoers rules, SUID binaries, file capabilities, cron jobs, and exposed credentials.
- [Active Directory Enumeration Cheat Sheet: LDAP, Kerberos & SMB](https://oopsmypassword.web.app/cheatsheets/active-directory-enumeration-cheatsheet): Authorized Active Directory security assessment commands for SMB signing checks, BloodHound collection, SPN Kerberoasting, and AD CS auditing.
- [Shodan Search Filters Cheat Sheet: Attack Surface & OSINT](https://oopsmypassword.web.app/cheatsheets/shodan-search-filters-cheatsheet): Complete reference of Shodan query filters (org, asn, ssl.cert, http.favicon.hash, vuln, product) for external attack-surface monitoring.
- [HTTP Security Headers Cheat Sheet: CSP, HSTS & CORS Hardening](https://oopsmypassword.web.app/cheatsheets/http-security-headers-cheatsheet): Copy-ready HTTP response headers (Strict-Transport-Security, Content-Security-Policy, X-Frame-Options, Permissions-Policy) and curl audit commands.
- [Incident Response First-Hour Cheat Sheet: Triage & Containment](https://oopsmypassword.web.app/cheatsheets/incident-response-first-hour-cheatsheet): First-hour Linux & account compromise triage checklist: preserving volatile network/process state, isolating hosts, and revoking active sessions.

## Security Glossary Terms
- [k-Anonymity](https://oopsmypassword.web.app/glossary/k-anonymity): k-Anonymity is a privacy property where a lookup or record cannot be distinguished from at least k-1 other items in the same set, allowing breach checks without revealing the secret queried.
- [Argon2id](https://oopsmypassword.web.app/glossary/argon2id): Argon2id is the modern winner of the Password Hashing Competition that combines memory-hard resistance against GPU cracking (Argon2d) with side-channel timing resistance (Argon2i).
- [Credential Stuffing](https://oopsmypassword.web.app/glossary/credential-stuffing): Credential stuffing is an automated cyberattack where bots replay millions of leaked username-and-password pairs from one data breach across other websites to hijack accounts that reused the same password.
- [Password Spraying](https://oopsmypassword.web.app/glossary/password-spraying): Password spraying is a low-and-slow authentication attack that tests one common password (such as Summer2026! or Welcome123) across thousands of user accounts to avoid triggering per-account lockout thresholds.
- [Passkey (FIDO2 / WebAuthn)](https://oopsmypassword.web.app/glossary/passkey-webauthn): A passkey is a phishing-resistant digital credential based on FIDO2 and WebAuthn public-key cryptography that replaces passwords with a cryptographic key pair bound to the website genuine domain.
- [TOTP (Time-Based One-Time Password)](https://oopsmypassword.web.app/glossary/totp-rfc-6238): TOTP (RFC 6238) is an offline two-factor authentication algorithm that computes a short-lived 6- to 8-digit code from a shared secret key and the current Unix timestamp, rotating every 30 seconds.
- [Browser-in-the-Browser (BitB) Phishing](https://oopsmypassword.web.app/glossary/browser-in-the-browser-bitb): Browser-in-the-Browser (BitB) is a phishing technique that renders a fake HTML/CSS popup window inside a webpage to imitate a legitimate Google, Microsoft, or Apple OAuth login dialog complete with a spoofed HTTPS address bar.
- [IDOR (Insecure Direct Object Reference)](https://oopsmypassword.web.app/glossary/idor-insecure-direct-object-reference): Insecure Direct Object Reference (IDOR), a form of Broken Object Level Authorization (BOLA), occurs when an application uses a client-supplied identifier (such as ?invoice_id=1042) to fetch or modify a record without verifying that the logged-in user owns that object.
- [SSRF (Server-Side Request Forgery)](https://oopsmypassword.web.app/glossary/ssrf-server-side-request-forgery): Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF) is a web vulnerability where an attacker tricks a backend server into making HTTP or network requests to internal-only services, localhost ports, or cloud metadata endpoints.
- [XSS (Cross-Site Scripting)](https://oopsmypassword.web.app/glossary/xss-cross-site-scripting): Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) is an injection vulnerability where untrusted data is rendered into a web page without context-aware output encoding, allowing an attacker to execute arbitrary JavaScript in another user browser session.
- [SQL Injection (SQLi)](https://oopsmypassword.web.app/glossary/sql-injection-sqli): SQL Injection (SQLi) is a critical vulnerability where user input is concatenated directly into a database query string, allowing an attacker to alter the SQL syntax and read, modify, or delete arbitrary database data.
- [CSRF (Cross-Site Request Forgery)](https://oopsmypassword.web.app/glossary/csrf-cross-site-request-forgery): Cross-Site Request Forgery (CSRF) is an attack that tricks an authenticated user browser into sending an unwanted state-changing HTTP request (such as changing an email or transferring funds) to a web application where they are currently signed in.
- [JWT (JSON Web Token)](https://oopsmypassword.web.app/glossary/jwt-json-web-token): A JSON Web Token (JWT, RFC 7519) is a compact, URL-safe token format consisting of a Base64URL-encoded JSON Header, Payload (claims), and cryptographic Signature separated by dots.
- [Subdomain Takeover](https://oopsmypassword.web.app/glossary/subdomain-takeover): Subdomain takeover occurs when a subdomain (such as promo.example.com) has a dangling DNS CNAME or A record pointing to an external cloud resource (S3 bucket, GitHub Pages, Azure App) that has been deleted or unclaimed, allowing an attacker to register that cloud resource and serve content under the organization legitimate subdomain.
- [Google Dorking (Search Engine Recon)](https://oopsmypassword.web.app/glossary/google-dorking): Google Dorking (Google Hacking) is the use of advanced search engine operators—such as site:, filetype:, inurl:, intitle:, and intext:—to locate publicly indexed configuration files, exposed directories, login portals, and sensitive documents.
- [IDN Homograph Attack (Punycode Spoofing)](https://oopsmypassword.web.app/glossary/idn-homograph-attack): An IDN homograph attack registers a domain name containing non-ASCII Unicode characters (such as Cyrillic "а" instead of Latin "a") that look visually identical to a trusted brand domain in order to deceive users into visiting a phishing site.
- [Typosquatting & Combo-Squatting](https://oopsmypassword.web.app/glossary/typosquatting): Typosquatting (and combo-squatting) is the registration of lookalike domains that differ from a trusted brand by a single mistyped letter, character swap (rn vs m), or appended keyword (such as microsoft-security-login.com) for phishing or malware delivery.
- [Zero Trust Architecture (ZTA)](https://oopsmypassword.web.app/glossary/zero-trust-architecture): Zero Trust Architecture (NIST SP 800-207) is a security model that eliminates implicit trust based on network location ("inside the corporate LAN/VPN") and instead requires continuous authentication, authorization, and encryption for every user, device, and service request.
- [Privilege Escalation](https://oopsmypassword.web.app/glossary/privilege-escalation): Privilege escalation is the act of exploiting a bug, misconfiguration, or weak permission to gain higher access rights—either vertically (from a standard user or web service account to root/SYSTEM) or horizontally (accessing another user account of the same tier).
- [Lateral Movement](https://oopsmypassword.web.app/glossary/lateral-movement): Lateral movement refers to the techniques an attacker uses after compromising one endpoint to pivot across the internal network to other workstations, servers, and domain controllers in search of high-value assets.
- [Kerberoasting](https://oopsmypassword.web.app/glossary/kerberoasting): Kerberoasting is an Active Directory post-exploitation technique where any authenticated domain user requests Kerberos TGS service tickets for accounts with Service Principal Names (SPNs) and cracks those tickets offline to recover the service account cleartext password.
- [Canary Token (Honeytoken)](https://oopsmypassword.web.app/glossary/canary-token): A Canary Token (or honeytoken) is a decoy credential, fake API key, tracked document, or unique DNS/HTTP URL planted in sensitive systems that has no legitimate operational use—so any access immediately alerts defenders to an active intrusion.
- [CVE & CVSS Score](https://oopsmypassword.web.app/glossary/cve-and-cvss): CVE (Common Vulnerabilities and Exposures) is the standardized global identifier for publicly disclosed security flaws (e.g., CVE-2026-0768), while CVSS (Common Vulnerability Scoring System) rates technical severity from 0.0 to 10.0.
- [SIEM & SOAR](https://oopsmypassword.web.app/glossary/siem-and-soar): SIEM (Security Information and Event Management) aggregates, normalizes, and correlates security logs across an organization to detect threats, while SOAR (Security Orchestration, Automation, and Response) automates triage playbooks and containment actions.
- [EDR & XDR (Endpoint Detection & Response)](https://oopsmypassword.web.app/glossary/edr-and-xdr): EDR (Endpoint Detection and Response) continuously monitors workstation and server process trees, memory, file changes, and network sockets to detect and contain behavioral threats, while XDR extends that correlation across identity, cloud, and network layers.
- [CORS Misconfiguration](https://oopsmypassword.web.app/glossary/cors-misconfiguration): A Cross-Origin Resource Sharing (CORS) misconfiguration occurs when a server dynamically reflects an arbitrary Origin header in Access-Control-Allow-Origin alongside Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true, allowing malicious websites to read authenticated API responses.
- [Banner Grabbing](https://oopsmypassword.web.app/glossary/shodan-banner-grabbing): Banner grabbing is the technique of reading the initial handshake or response headers returned by a network service (such as SSH, HTTP, SMTP, or FTP) to identify the software product, version number, and operating system.
- [SBOM (Software Bill of Materials)](https://oopsmypassword.web.app/glossary/sbom-software-bill-of-materials): A Software Bill of Materials (SBOM) is a machine-readable inventory (in CycloneDX or SPDX format) listing every open-source and third-party library, version, and transitive dependency packaged inside an application.
- [Diceware Passphrase](https://oopsmypassword.web.app/glossary/diceware-passphrase): Diceware is a provably random method for generating strong, memorable passphrases by selecting random words from a numbered word list using physical dice or a browser CSPRNG.
- [CSPRNG (Cryptographically Secure PRNG)](https://oopsmypassword.web.app/glossary/csprng): A Cryptographically Secure Pseudo-Random Number Generator (CSPRNG) produces unpredictable random bytes seeded by operating-system hardware entropy, suitable for generating passwords, cryptographic keys, and session tokens.
